εἰδωλόθυτον καὶ νομίζοντος ὅτι ἔστι τι εἰδωλόθυτον. 1 Kor 10,26 Ἃ ἐσθίετε τοῦ
κυρίου ἐστίν, ἐπεὶ καὶ ἡ γῆ καὶ πάντα ὅσων πεπλήρωται. 260 1 Kor 10,31 Πάντα
πεφυλαγμένως ποιεῖτε, ἵνα δοξάζωσι δι' ὑμᾶς τὸν θεὸν καὶ μὴ σκανδαλίζωνται. 1
Kor 10,32 Μὴ αἴτιοι προσκόμματος γίνεσθε Ἰουδαίοις καὶ Ἕλλησιν ἐν τῷ μὴ
προφάσει τῆς κακῆς ὑμῶν ἀναστροφῆς φεύγειν αὐτοὺς τὴν πίστιν, τῇ δὲ ἐκκλησίᾳ
τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν τῷ τοὺς ὀλιγοπίστους μὴ σκανδαλίζεσθαι. 1 Kor 11,2 Ἐπαινεῖ νῦν καίπερ
διεσφαλμένους, ἵνα κἂν τοῦ λοιποῦ πεισθῶσιν οἷς λέγει. 1 Kor 11,3 Προτρεπόμενος
μᾶλλον ἢ ἀποδεχόμενος λέγει, ἵνα ἑξῆς τὴν παραίνεσιν βεβαιώσῃ ἐν αὐτοῖς· θέλω δὲ
ὑμᾶς εἰδέναι ὅτι παντὸς ἀνδρὸς ἡ κεφαλὴ ὁ Χριστός ἐστιν, κεφαλὴ δὲ γυναικὸς ὁ
ἀνήρ, κεφαλὴ δὲ Χριστοῦ ὁ θεός. Εἰ ἀσεβῶς ἐκλαμβάνοι τις, κατὰ τὸν τῆς θεότητος
λόγον, εἰ δὲ εὐσεβῶς, κατὰ τὸν τῆς οἰκονομίας· οὐ γὰρ περὶ τοῦ γεγενῆσθαι νῦν ὁ
λόγος–ἰδοὺ γὰρ ὁ ἀνὴρ τὴν γυναῖκα οὐκ ἐποίησεν–οὐδὲ ἡ τάξις ᾗ ἐχρήσατο Παῦλος
εἰς τοῦτο βλέπει, ἀλλ' εἰς μόνην τὴν ὑποταγήν· οὐ διὰ τὴν τῆς φύσεως ἀλλοτρίωσιν–
καὶ ὅλως οὐδὲ τοῦ μονογενοῦς ἡ θεότης λαμβάνεται νῦν, ἀλλ' ἡ οἰκονομία
ἐγγυτέρω ἔχουσα πρὸς τὸν ἄνδρα καὶ τὴν γυναῖκα κατὰ τὴν φύσιν. Ἐπειδὴ οἱ Ἀρείου
λέγουσιν· ὥσπερ κεφαλὴ τοῦ ἀνδρὸς ὁ Χριστός, ἐπειδὴ ποιητὴς αὐτοῦ ἐστιν, οὕτω
τοῦ Χριστοῦ ὁ θεὸς ὡς ποιητὴς αὐτοῦ, δοκοῦσι τὰ ἑξῆς ἀγνοεῖν· τῆς γὰρ γυναικὸς
κεφαλὴ ὁ ἀνήρ. καὶ οὔτε ποιητὴς αὐτῆς ἐστιν καὶ ὁμοούσιος αὐτῇ ἐστιν, καὶ κατὰ
τὸν αὐτὸν λόγον εὑρισκόμεθα ὁμοούσιοι τῷ Χριστῷ. οὕτω πάντα πᾶσι ληροῦσιν.
κεφαλὴ γὰρ ὧδε κατὰ τὸ ἀρχοντικὸν εἴρηται, οὐ κατὰ τὸ ποιητικόν· ὥστε ὁ ἔχων
ἄρχοντα καὶ κεφαλὴν τὸν Χριστόν, ἐὰν ἁμαρτῇ, τὸν ἑαυτοῦ ἄρχοντα ὑβρίζει. κατὰ
τοῦτον τὸν λόγον τῷ Χριστῷ ὑποτεταγμένοι τῷ θεῷ καὶ πατρὶ ὑποτετάγμεθα, ὅτι καὶ
τοῦ Χριστοῦ κεφαλὴ ὁ θεός. 261 1 Kor 11,4 Προφητεύειν λέγει τὸ τοὺς προφήτας
ἑρμηνεύειν. ἤτοι ἐν τούτῳ ἡ διαφορὰ τῶν πάλαι προφητῶν καὶ τῶν νέων, ὅτι οἱ μὲν
παλαιοὶ γενικώτερον ἐπροφήτευον περὶ ἐκπτώσεως Ἰουδαίων καὶ κλήσεως ἐθνῶν
καὶ τῆς ἐνσάρκου ἐπιδημίας Χριστοῦ, οἱ δὲ ἰδικῶς ὡς ἐπὶ Ἀνανίου ὁ Πέτρος. 1 Kor
11,7 Ἐκ τούτων φαίνεται ὅτι οὔτε κατὰ τὴν ψυχὴν εἰκὼν θεοῦ ἄνθρωπος, οὔτε κατὰ
τὸ σῶμα. εἰ γὰρ ἦν καθ' ἕν τι τούτων, πάντως ἂν καὶ ἡ γυνὴ εἰκὼν θεοῦ ἐκλήθη, καὶ
αὐτὴ τὸν τύπον ἔχουσα τὸν τοῦ σώματος καὶ τὴν ψυχὴν ἔχουσα οἵαν καὶ ὁ ἀνήρ. εἰ
δὲ τὴν αὐτὴν ἔχουσα ἡ γυνὴ τῷ ἀνδρὶ ψυχὴν καὶ σάρκα εἰκὼν οὐ λέγεται, δηλονότι
κατὰ τὸ ἀρχικὸν εἰκὼν θεοῦ ὁ ἄνθρωπος. ὅτε μὲν γὰρ περὶ τῶν ἀλόγων ὁ λόγος, καὶ
ἡ γυνὴ εἰκὼν θεοῦ· ὅτε δὲ ἡ ἐξέτασις ἀνδρὸς πρὸς γυναῖκας, μόνος εἰκὼν ὁ ἀνήρ,
διότι τὸ ἄρρεν καὶ θῆλυ ἐν ἀνθρώποις πάντων κρατεῖ τῶν ἐν γῇ, τῶν ἐν θαλάσσῃ,
τῶν ἐν ἀέρι, γυναικὸς δὲ ὁ ἀνήρ, ἀνδρὸς δὲ οὐδεὶς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς. ὡς οὖν οὐδεὶς ἄρχει
θεοῦ ἐν τοῖς οὖσιν, οὕτως οὐδὲ ἀνδρὸς ἐν τοῖς ἐπιγείοις. φύσιν δὲ νοοῦμεν ἡμεῖς τῶν
πραγμάτων αὐτῶν τὴν ἀλήθειαν. Εἰκών ἐστιν ὁ ἀνὴρ τοῦ θεοῦ, οὐ κατὰ σῶμα ἢ
ψυχήν, ἀλλὰ κατὰ τὸ ἀρχικόν· ἔχει γὰρ μετὰ τῶν ἄλλων ἐν ὑποταγῇ καὶ τὴν
γυναῖκα, καὶ ὥσπερ οὐδεὶς ἄρχει θεοῦ ἐν τοῖς οὖσιν, οὕτως οὔτε ἀνδρὸς ἐν τοῖς
ἐπιγείοις. ὥσπερ δὲ καλῶς ὑπακούων ὁ ἀνὴρ τῷ ἀρχηγέτῃ δόξα καὶ ἔπαινος θεοῦ
ἐστιν, οὕτως καὶ ἡ γυνὴ δόξα τοῦ ἀνδρός ἐστιν καλῶς αὐτῷ ὑποτεταγμένη. 1 Kor
11,10 Τὸ τραχὺ καὶ δύσεικτον τῶν γυναικῶν συνεωρακὼς ὁ ἀπόστολός φησιν,
ὑπομιμνήσκων ὅτι καὶ ἀγγέλους ἐπέστησεν ἡμῖν ὁ θεός. τινὲς δὲ ἀγγέλους τοὺς
ἱερέας τῆς ἐκκλησίας εἰρῆσθαί φασιν καὶ δι' αὐτοὺς καλύπτεσθαι ὡς μὴ λαβούσας
τοῦ ἄρχειν τὴν ἐλευθερίαν. τοῦτο 262 δὲ ἴσως εἶπεν, ἐπειδὴ καὶ γυναῖκες
προεφήτευον ἐκ πνεύματος ἁγίου. τοῦ δὲ πνεύματος ἐνεργοῦντος πᾶσα ἀνάγκη τοὺς
λειτουργοὺς ἀγγέλους παρεῖναι, καὶ δεῖ διὰ τοῦτο κατακαλύπτεσθαι τὴν γυναῖκα. 1
Kor 11,14–15 Οὐκ ἀπὸ τοῦ παλαιοῦ ἔθους ἀλλ' ἀπὸ τοῦ κατ' αὐτοὺς ἐδοκίμασε τοῦτο.
καὶ οἱ κομῶντες τὸ παλαιὸν ἐκ μέρους ἀποκείροντες ἐπὶ πλεῖον ἢ ἔδει κομῶντες,
γυναικὶ δὲ ἀεὶ τὸ κείρεσθαι ἀπεδοκιμάσθη. 1 Kor 11,19 Αἱρέσεις λέγει οὐ τὰς ἐν τοῖς
δόγμασιν ἀλλὰ τὰς ἐν ἔθεσι καὶ τύποις. 1 Kor 11,–21 Ἐγκαλεῖ ὅτι συνερχόμενοι ὡς
ἐπὶ κοινωνίᾳ τοῦ ἁγίου σώματος οὐκ ἀνέμενον ἀλλήλους, ἀλλά τινων διαπενίαν
ἀσχολουμένων καὶ ὑστερούντων προφθάνοντες οἱ εὔποροι οὐκ ἀνέμενον τοὺς
ἄλλους, ἀλλ' ὑπὸ γαστριμαργίας τοῦ μὲν κυριακοῦ δείπνου παρημέλουν, ἐπὶ δὲ τὰ
pass_a_gloss: [10:25 note, continued] ...the idol-sacrifice and thinking that idol-sacrifice is something. [Label 1 Kor 10,26] The things you eat are the Lord's, since also the earth and all things with which it has been filled. [Label 1 Kor 10,31] Do all things guardedly, so that they may glorify God because of you and not be made to stumble. [Label 1 Kor 10,32] Do not become causes of stumbling to Jews and Greeks, in their not fleeing the faith on the pretext of your bad conduct, and to the church of God, in those of little faith not being made to stumble. [Label 1 Kor 11,2] He praises now although they have erred, so that at least for the rest [of time] they may be persuaded by what he says. [Label 1 Kor 11,3] He speaks exhorting rather than approving, so that next he may make firm the exhortation in them: 'but I want you to know that the head of every man is Christ, and the head of woman the man, and the head of Christ God.' If someone takes it impiously, [it is] according to the principle of the godhead; but if piously, according to that of the economy; for the discussion now is not about having been made (look, the man did not make the woman), nor does the order which Paul used look to this, but to subordination alone; not because of an estrangement of nature; and in general the godhead of the only-begotten is not taken now, but the economy, which stands nearer to the man and the woman according to nature. Since the [followers] of Arius say: as Christ is head of the man since he is his maker, so God is [head] of Christ as his maker, they seem not to know what follows: for the head of the woman is the man. And he is neither her maker and he is of one substance with her, and according to the same reasoning we are found of one substance with Christ. So they talk nonsense in everything. For 'head' here is said according to ruling, not according to making; so that the one having Christ as ruler and head, if he sins, insults his own ruler. According to this reasoning, subject to Christ we are subject to God and Father, because God is also the head of Christ. [Label 1 Kor 11,4] He calls prophesying the interpreting of the prophets. Or the difference of the old prophets and the new is in this, that the old prophesied more generally about the falling away of Jews and calling of nations and the enfleshed coming of Christ, but the [new] ones particularly, as Peter in the case of Ananias. [Label 1 Kor 11,7] From these it appears that man is image of God neither according to the soul nor according to the body. For if he were according to some one of these, entirely the woman too would have been called image of God, she too having the form of the body and having a soul such as the man has. But if the woman, having the same soul and flesh as the man, is not called image, clearly man is image of God according to rule. For when the discussion is about the irrational [creatures], the woman too is image of God; but when the examination is of man toward women, the man alone is image, because the male and female among humans rule all things on the earth, in the sea, in the air, and the man [rules] the woman, but no one on the earth [rules] the man. So as no one among existing things rules God, so neither [does anyone rule] man among earthly things. And we understand nature as the truth of the things themselves. [Second form, not printed again: The man is image of God, not according to body or soul, but according to rule; for he has with the others the woman too in subjection, and as no one among existing things rules God, so neither [anyone] the man among earthly things.] [Second form, printed as an addition] And as the man, obeying the leader well, is glory and praise of God, so also the woman, well subjected to him, is glory of the man. [Label 1 Kor 11,10] The apostle speaks having observed the roughness and unyieldingness of women, reminding that God has set angels too over us. And some say that the priests of the church are called angels and that because of them [women] are veiled, as not having received the freedom of ruling. Perhaps he said this since women too prophesied from the Holy Spirit. And when the Spirit is at work, there is every necessity for the ministering angels to be present, and because of this the woman must be veiled. [Label 1 Kor 11,14-15] Not from the old custom but from the one in their time he judged this. Even those wearing long hair of old, cutting off in part, wearing long hair more than was needed; but for a woman to be shorn was always disapproved. [Label 1 Kor 11,19] He calls factions not those in doctrines but those in customs and patterns. [Label 1 Kor 11,-21] He accuses [them] that, coming together as for the communion of the holy body, they did not wait for one another, but while some were busy on account of poverty and coming late, the well-off, getting ahead, did not wait for the others, but from gluttony they neglected the Lord's supper, and to the... pass_b_english: …idol food, and who thinks that idol food is something.
On 1 Corinthians 10:26: What you eat belongs to the Lord, since the earth does too, and everything that fills it.
On 1 Corinthians 10:31: Do everything with care, so that people give glory to God because of you and do not stumble.

On 1 Corinthians 10:32: Do not become a cause of stumbling to Jews and Greeks: see that they do not flee the faith with your bad conduct as their excuse. Nor to the church of God: see that those of little faith are not made to stumble.
On 1 Corinthians 11:2: He praises them now, though they have gone wrong, so that from here on they may at least be persuaded by what he says.

On 1 Corinthians 11:3: He speaks to spur them on rather than to approve them, so that he can then make his exhortation firm in them: “But I want you to know that the head of every man is Christ, the head of a woman is the man, and the head of Christ is God.” Read impiously, this is taken as speaking of the Godhead; read piously, of the saving plan. The subject here is not being made (look: the man did not make the woman), and the order Paul used does not have that in view. It looks only to subordination, not to any difference of nature. In general, what is in view here is not the Godhead of the Only-begotten but the saving plan, which stands closer by nature to the man and the woman.

The followers of Arius say, “As Christ is head of the man because he is his maker, so God is head of Christ as his maker.” They seem not to know what comes next: “the head of the woman is the man.” He is not her maker, and he is of one substance with her; and on the same reasoning we turn out to be of one substance with Christ. So they talk nonsense about everything. “Head” is used here in the sense of ruling, not of making. So whoever has Christ as ruler and head insults his own ruler when he sins. On this reasoning, by being subject to Christ we are subject to God the Father, because God is also the head of Christ.

On 1 Corinthians 11:4: By “prophesying” he means interpreting the prophets. Or else the difference between the prophets of old and the new ones lies here: the old prophets spoke in general terms about the Jews' falling away, the calling of the nations and Christ's coming in the flesh, while the new ones spoke of particular cases, as Peter did with Ananias.

On 1 Corinthians 11:7: From these words it appears that man is the image of God neither in his soul nor in his body. If he were the image in either of these, the woman too would certainly have been called the image of God, since she too has the form of a body and a soul like the man's. If the woman has the same soul and flesh as the man and is still not called the image, then clearly man is the image of God in his rule. When the discussion concerns the creatures without reason, the woman too is the image of God. But when man is weighed against women, the man alone is the image, because male and female among human beings rule over everything on the earth, in the sea and in the air, while the man rules over the woman, and no one on earth rules over the man. As nothing that exists rules over God, so nothing on earth rules over the man. By “nature” we understand the truth of the things themselves.
The second catena form adds: Just as the man who obeys his Sovereign well is the glory and praise of God, so the woman who is rightly subject to him is the glory of the man.

On 1 Corinthians 11:10: The apostle says this because he has seen how rough and unyielding women are, and he reminds them that God has also set angels over us. Some say that the priests of the church are called “angels” here, and that women cover their heads because of them, since women have not been given the freedom to rule. Perhaps he said this because women too used to prophesy by the Holy Spirit. When the Spirit is at work, the ministering angels must be present, and so the woman must cover her head.

On 1 Corinthians 11:14–15: He judged this not by ancient custom but by the custom of their own day. Even those who wore their hair long in the old days cut part of it off, though they wore it longer than they should have; but for a woman to be shorn was always disapproved.
On 1 Corinthians 11:19: By “factions” he means not factions over doctrine but factions over customs and practices.

On 1 Corinthians 11:20–21: He rebukes them because, when they came together as if for communion in the holy body, they did not wait for one another.
